Subject: Discovery recap & proposed POC scope — Catalyst Analytics

Hi Liam / Sofia —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed POC plan so we all have the same expectations. Please call out anything I missed.

Pain points you described:
- Model hallucination on domain-specific financial docs (quarterly statements, M&A memos) causing extra manual QA.
- High per-request cost and inconsistent latency for interactive analyst workflows.
- Need for guarded access controls and audit logs for regulated customers.

Primary goals for a successful POC (what success looks like):
1) Reduce hallucination/incorrect extractions by measurable margin vs current baseline (target: 40% reduction in post-editing).
2) Maintain 95th pct latency < 600ms for short interactive queries.
3) Demonstrate role-based access + audit trail for all inference requests.

Proposed scope (4-week POC):
- Week 0: access & environment setup (VPC peering or dedicated private endpoint).
- Week 1: ingest 2 sample document sets (~2K docs), configure prompt set and eval harness.
- Week 2: run evaluation against agreed prompt set, iterate on chaining and guardrails.
- Week 3: throughput/latency tuning and mock analyst sessions.
- Week 4: acceptance run and final metrics + technical review.

Owners (Redwood):
- Sean Gallagher (Account lead) — kickoff scheduling, SOW & procurement alignment.
- Dev Patel (Platform engineer) — environment access, private endpoint setup, keys.
- Grace O'Connor (Solutions / Evals) — prompt set, eval harness, acceptance criteria.

Asks from Catalyst to start (first two items block us):
1) A small sample of representative documents (anonymized) and one canonical prompt for extraction tasks.
2) Contact for procurement and whether you need our standard SOW or a partner addendum.
3) Security questionnaire if you have one; we can fill and return.

Attached: draft POC SOW (POC_SOW_draft.pdf).

Proposed kickoff window: Apr 19–21 (we can shift by a week if needed).
Next step: if this looks right, I’ll circulate a short mutual action plan and book the kickoff.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

Sean — thanks for the tidy recap. This matches our internal notes; a few clarifications and one small ask before we lock dates: 

1) Scope: we like the focus on hallucination reduction. Can we tighten the ingest to 1,200 docs for the POC (we want faster iteration)?
2) Security: procurement wants clear answers on data residency (do you keep tokens/logs), and whether we can run in our AWS account (VPC) or must use Redwood-hosted.
3) Pricing / estimated spend: procurement also requested a ballpark cost for the 4-week run to include in the internal PO.

I’ve attached our standard procurement checklist (Procurement_Instructions_Catalyst.pdf) and copied Sofia (security/ops) who will lead on the security questionnaire.

If we can get a short note on logs/residency and a revised SOW with 1,200 docs, we can likely target Apr 19 kickoff.

Liam / Sofia — great, thanks. Quick answers and an updated plan below.

On your asks: 
- Ingest size: we’re fine with 1,200 docs for the POC; updated SOW will reflect that.
- Data residency / logs: Redwood does not persist raw customer documents beyond what’s required for the POC. We keep metadata/audit logs for requests (customer id, timestamp, model variant) for 90 days by default; audit retention can be extended on Dedicated/Private deployments. If you require the POC to run in your AWS account we can do a Private deployment with a customer-managed VPC endpoint — Dev, please confirm estimated setup time below.
- Ballpark cost: for a 4-week, 1,200-doc POC with private endpoint + 2 Engineer support hours/week we estimate ~$18k–22k. Legal/procurement line items will be itemized in the SOW.

Action items and owners: 
- Dev Patel (dev.patel@redwood.com) — confirm VPC peering steps and give ETA for private endpoint setup (Dev: can you comment if Apr 19 start is realistic?).
- Grace O'Connor (grace.oconnor@redwood.com) — will prepare the eval harness and initial prompt set; expect a short questionnaire to finalize acceptance metrics by Apr 12.
- Sean — I’ll revise the SOW (reflecting 1,200 docs and pricing) and share a DocuSign link for signature; I’ll also fill and attach Redwood's responses to your security questions (see attached redwood-security-questionnaire-filled.pdf).

Links: updated draft SOW and mutual action plan: https://drive.redwood.com/poctemplates/CAT-341-POC-SOW
